mn18:6.3: “Here, mendicants, in the morning I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Kapilavatthu for alms.
mn18:6.4: I wandered for alms in Kapilavatthu. After the meal, on my return from almsround, I went to the Great Wood for the day’s meditation.
mn18:6.5: I plunged deep into the Great Wood, and sat at the root of a young wood-apple tree to meditate.
mn18:6.6: Daṇḍapāṇi the Sakyan, mendicants, while going for a walk, also came to the Great Wood.
mn18:6.7: He plunged deep into the Great Wood and came to the young wood-apple tree where I was. He approached me and exchanged greetings with me.
mn18:6.8: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he stood to one side leaning on his staff. Standing to one side, mendicants, Daṇḍapāṇi the Sakyan said to me,
mn18:6.9: ‘What is the ascetic’s doctrine? What does he assert?’
mn18:6.10: When he had spoken, mendicants, I said to Daṇḍapāṇi the Sakyan,
mn18:6.11: ‘Respectable sir, my doctrine is such that one does not argue with anyone in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans. And it is such that perceptions do not underlie the brahmin who lives detached from sensual pleasures, without indecision, stripped of worry, and rid of craving for rebirth in this or that state.
mn18:6.12: That is my doctrine, and that is what I assert.’
mn18:6.13: When I had spoken, mendicants, Daṇḍapāṇi shook his head, waggled his tongue, raised his eyebrows until his brow puckered in three furrows, and left leaning on his staff.”
mn18:10.3: ‘Judgments driven by proliferating perceptions beset a person.
mn18:10.4: If they don’t find anything worth approving, welcoming, or getting attached to in the source from which these arise,
mn18:10.5: just this is the end of the underlying tendencies to desire …
mn18:10.6: This is where these bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.’
mn18:11.3: “Reverend Kaccāna, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
mn18:11.4: ‘Judgments driven by proliferating perceptions beset a person.
mn18:11.5: If they don’t find anything worth approving, welcoming, or getting attached to in the source from which these arise,
mn18:11.6: just this is the end of the underlying tendencies to desire …
mn18:11.7: This is where these bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.’
mn18:11.8: Reverend Kaccāna, soon after the Buddha left, we considered,
mn18:11.9: ‘Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
mn18:11.10: “Mendicant, judgments driven by proliferating perceptions beset a person.
mn18:11.11: If they don’t find anything worth approving, welcoming, or getting attached to in the source from which these arise,
mn18:11.12: just this is the end of the underlying tendencies to desire …
mn18:11.13: This is where these bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.”’
mn18:11.14: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?
mn18:11.16: ‘This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions. He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.
mn18:11.17: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.’

mn18:20.2: “Sir, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
mn18:20.3: ‘Judgments driven by proliferating perceptions beset a person.
mn18:20.4: If they don’t find anything worth approving, welcoming, or getting attached to in the source from which these arise,
mn18:20.5: just this is the end of the underlying tendencies to desire …
mn18:20.6: This is where these bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.’
mn18:20.7: Sir, soon after the Buddha left, we considered,
mn18:20.8: ‘Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
mn18:20.9: “Mendicant, judgments driven by proliferating perceptions beset a person.
mn18:20.10: If they don’t find anything worth approving, welcoming, or getting attached to in the source from which these arise,
mn18:20.11: just this is the end of the underlying tendencies to desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, the desire for continued existence, and ignorance. This is the end of taking up the rod and the sword, the end of quarrels, arguments, and disputes, of accusations, backbiting, and lies.
mn18:20.12: This is where these bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.”
mn18:20.13: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?’
mn18:20.15: ‘This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions. He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha. Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.’
mn18:20.16: So, sir, we went to Venerable Mahākaccāna and asked him about this matter.
